elements.element: No non-compete restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to prohibit the Company from participating in Internet projects similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to grant HDI the exclusive right to use the “Deerskin” brand for a self-contained direct-to-consumer website, restricting the Company’s use in that field.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The restriction is limited to the capitalized Deerskin Products term; references to products “substantially similar” to Deerskin Products and similar companies were deleted. The new carve-out also permits developing, offering, or selling products other than Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 expressly begins the restrictions with “during the term of this Agreement.”

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 adds that the restriction will apply “in no event for more than twelve (12) months following the Effective Date.”

elements.element: The restriction includes a carve-out for internal development.
elements.evidence: The added language states that Section 6.1 does not restrict the Company from “internally developing any product, catalog or web site.”

elements.element: The restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: The added language permits the Company to acquire, be acquired by, or continue operating the business of an entity engaged in offering apparel or accessories on the Internet.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because both a product-specific non-compete and a Deerskin-brand field-of-use exclusivity remain. It achieves every fallback element by narrowing the restriction to Deerskin Products, limiting it to the term and no more than 12 months, and adding operative internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. The changes are targeted and leave the unrelated termination and exclusivity framework effective.
